headline: Elon Musk has praised the memory chip maker Micron for fair pricing of future supply and said other suppliers had been extortionate.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a prominent buyer's public comment on memory pricing in a shortage, but one post with no rival named and no figures from Musk.
importance_line: A large buyer publicly praising one memory supplier and calling others extortionate shows how tense pricing has become in a shortage that feeds into what phones, computers and AI services cost, but Musk names no other supplier and gives no price, and it is one social media post.
summary: Benzinga reports that Elon Musk, chief executive of SpaceX, wrote on X on Tuesday 13 Oct that Micron Technology, the US memory chip maker, "has been reasonable regarding future memory prices, while others have been extortionate, which is something today's customers won't forget", naming no other supplier. He was replying to a post by Nicholas Mugalli, chief executive of World Trade Securities, about a JPMorgan note that says demand for memory runs well above supply and models shortages of about 20% in 2026, 19% in 2027 and 15% in 2028.
notes: Read from fulltext (Benzinga article carried by Yahoo Finance; the Yahoo link is the page read). The shortage figures are JPMorgan's forecast as reported by Benzinga.
